segments.title: Opening identification of the tape
segments.summary: The interviewer identifies the tape and Manuel Paul gives his name as Emmanuel Paul.

segments.title: Playing for amusement while holding a regular job
segments.summary: Paul says he played for amusement and felt the music, though the other musicians did not know it, because he held a regular job in those years.

segments.title: The car wreck with Thomas and Sam
segments.summary: The interviewer recalls an untaped story about a wreck; Paul says Sam got out of the car with Thomas and they could not see the oncoming car.

segments.title: Photo of Kid Thomas' band and the WPA band at the boys' home
segments.summary: They look at a c. 1955 photo of Kid Thomas' band, then a WPA band photo where Paul sits behind Willie Humphrey with his soprano sax; the band played at the boys' home on Wednesdays.

segments.title: Identifying WPA band members: conductor, saxes, clarinets, bass
segments.summary: Paul points out the conductor, Son Johnson, the two Eddie Johnsons, bassist Glennie, Howard Davis, Willie Humphrey, Henry Harden, Sidney Montague, Israel Gorman and Sam Lee.

segments.title: Identifying WPA banjo players, trumpets and other members
segments.summary: They name Landry, Andrew Morgan, Mike Lane on banjo, Sidney Cates, Leo Sanjay, Glapio, Crawford, Henry Russ, Louis the Man and McCullen, with Paul failing to recall some names.

segments.title: More unrecalled names, Shots and Hoods the banjo player; 111 musicians
segments.summary: Paul struggles over names, finds Shots and the tall banjoist Hoods, and notes there were about 111 musicians on the project.

segments.title: February 1935 photo on Dumaine Street; rehearsals and Ernest Pinn
segments.summary: A February 1935 photo of the band was taken on Dumaine Street near the boxing arena where they rehearsed; Paul praises banjoist Ernest Pinn, who lost his mind and died.

segments.title: Finding Paul in the picture and naming guitarist, bassists and trombones
segments.summary: Paul finds himself in the photo, they identify a guitarist, the many banjos, Glenny, Dave Morrison, Prince Bacturo and trombonist Harris.

segments.title: Preserving the historic WPA photograph
segments.summary: They discuss copying the photo at Tulane; Paul calls it a historic shot with every musician in the city of that time.

segments.title: Identifying the clarinet players: Bundy, Frank Crump, Howard Davis
segments.summary: Paul names clarinetists including Israel Gorman, Willie Humphrey, Bundy (now a cab driver), Frank Crump and Howard Davis, and a trumpeter who worked with him at the Y.

segments.title: Earlier 1931 photo and Louis Domaine
segments.summary: In a photo from about 1931 Paul had a sax, though it was another man's tenor horn; he identifies Louis Domaine at the right.

segments.title: Who directed the WPA band, and cutting it down to c. 1938
segments.summary: Louis Domaine directed the band while another man ran the project and picked out bad notes; the band was cut down around 1938. They talk about framing and keeping the photos.

segments.title: City Park concerts in white uniforms
segments.summary: A photo of the big band in City Park shows summer concerts in white seersucker uniforms, dated around 1937-38.

segments.title: Other photographs: graves, cafe, Paul's family
segments.summary: They look at snapshots including Joe Avery's grave, a cafe, Paul's granddaughter, daughter and his son, a pharmacist in Missouri.

segments.title: Closing the interview
segments.summary: The interviewer asks if Paul has anything to add; he says he could talk until morning but there is nothing more.
